uncited: This family encompasses techniques designed to optimize the Direct Volume Ray Casting (D2VR) pipeline on Graphics Processing Units (GPUs) by leveraging hardware-specific features such as early Z-culling.
The primary problem it solves is the computational bottleneck inherent in fragment-based volume rendering, where the high cost of shading often negates the benefits of hardware occlusion culling.

What sets this family apart is its focus on the ratio between computational effort per fragment and the potential for early termination; methods are evaluated based on how effectively their shading complexity interacts with early Z-cull mechanisms to achieve interactive or near-interactive rendering speeds.
The core principle shared by all methods in this family is the exploitation of the GPU's early Z-cull mechanism.
Early Z-culling discards fragments that are occluded by previously rendered fragments closer to the camera, thereby saving shading computations.
However, the effectiveness of this optimization is contingent upon the computational effort required per fragment.
The spreading method distributes volume data across multiple fragments or uses a rendering approach that results in a longer, more computationally intensive fragment shader.
The projective texture method maps volume data onto geometric primitives using texture mapping, imposing relatively light rendering efforts on individual fragments.
It is chosen for simpler shading requirements or when hardware texture sampling is highly optimized.
